summary: John Daishin Buksbazen works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles under Taizan Maezumi and Bernie Glassman.

Philosopher John Dewey studied at Burlington High School, the University of Vermont (~1875-1879), and Johns Hopkins University (~1882-1884). He held posts at the universities of Michigan, Minnesota, Chicago, and Columbia (~1904-1930).

Indologist and linguist John Dowson studied under Edwin Norris. He held positions at the East India Company College (~1855-1858), the Royal Asiatic Society, Staff College, Camberley (1855-1877), and University College London (1855-1877).

John E. Cort is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who earned degrees from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970-1974) and Harvard University (~1979-1984). He served as a professor at Denison University (~1993-2021).

Historian and Indologist John F. Richards studied at the University of New Hampshire (~1957-1961) and UC Berkeley (~1964-1970). He held academic posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968-1977) and Duke University (~1977-2007).

Indologist and historian John Faithfull Fleet studied at Merchant Taylors' School and University College London. He served in the Indian Civil Service (1865-1897), the Bombay Civil Service, and as Epigraphist for the Government of India (1883-1886).
John Fraser studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1903-1906). He held academic posts at the University of Aberdeen (~1906-1921) and the University of Oxford (~1921-1945).

Specializing in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Hangin studied at Hokkaido, Columbia, and Indiana universities. He taught at Johns Hopkins, UC Berkeley, Georgetown, Columbia, and Indiana University (1965-1989), and founded the Mongolia Society.
John H. Berthrong works in Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alfonso Verdu and held a post at Boston University (attested 1996).
Historian and Indologist John Henry Hutton was educated at Chigwell School and Worcester College, Oxford (~1903-1908). He served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1909 to 1936.

Classicist and linguist John Henry Wright studied at Dartmouth and Leipzig under Georg Curtius. He held professorships at Ohio State, Dartmouth, Johns Hopkins, the American School of Classical Studies at Athens, and Harvard University (~1887-1908).
Working in Indology and history, John Herbert Harington served as secretary (1790) and president (1825-1828) of The Asiatic Society, and as an honorary professor at Fort William College (~1801-1819).
John Hope studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1740-1750) and later held an academic post there from approximately 1761 to 1786.

John J. Holder, who works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, studied under Harry Krebs. He has held appointments at St. Norbert College (attested 2006, 2018) and a visiting research post at the University of Oxford.

Makransky works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, having studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and under numerous Tibetan teachers. He has held posts at Boston College, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar John James Jones studied at Aberystwyth University (~1912-1915). He later served as Deputy-Keeper of the Department of Printed Books at the National Library of Wales (~1926-1957).

Scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology John Jorgensen held research and teaching positions at the Australian National University, Griffith University, and the China Studies Research Centre at La Trobe University (attested 2019).

Historian, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar John Kieschnick held a post at the University of Bristol (~2005-2011) before becoming Professor of Buddhist Studies at Stanford University in ~2011.

Philosopher John Lane Bell studied at Lick-Wilmerding High School and the University of Oxford (~1963-1968). He held posts at the London School of Economics (~1968-1989), the National University of Singapore (~1988-1989), and the University of Western Ontario (~1989).

Indologist and art historian John Lockwood Kipling studied at Woodhouse Grove School. He taught at Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art, was principal of the National College of Arts, and curated the Lahore Museum (1875-1893).
